hypothesis: Exact-route zero-signal clocks should use the historical cadence of each route's active V57 execution directions.
decision: Retain every predeclared clock duration. Correct the SPCX sensitivity from the retired both-side cadence to the active short-only cadence of 2.164568081991215 trades per week. The seven-day threshold still represents approximately two expected short trades and therefore does not change.
falsifier: Replace this revision if exact prospective V57 evidence materially changes a route's attributable arrival process, if the live directional scope changes, or if checkpoint coverage becomes incomplete.
problem_restatement: The first cadence artifact used all SPCX development trades even though V57 authorizes only SPCX shorts. This changed descriptive expected-event and zero-event sensitivities but did not invalidate the seven-day review duration.

superseded_source_artifact.reason: SPCX sensitivity used both-side rather than active short-only development cadence

selection_rule.description: Choose a bounded review horizon corresponding to roughly two or more events under the frozen active-direction historical cadence where feasible.

hip3_spcx_cash_open_gap_reversal_bidirec.historical_cadence: 11 development short trades over the frozen 35.57-day development window; long authority is contained in V57

limitations: Historical cadence may not remain stationary under the current regime.
The Poisson calculation is a transparent sensitivity, not a validated arrival model or rejection threshold.
Cash-session holidays and shared-asset route overlap are not modeled by elapsed wall-clock time.
A due review requests diagnosis only; it is not evidence that a strategy is broken.
An observed eligible signal closes the zero-signal clock but does not establish execution quality or profitability.
